answer: A harbor registry can require every agent to lock a refundable stake before trading, like a ship posting bond before docking. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs real capital per identity, and misbehavior forfeits the bond. Reputation accrues slowly, like a glacier, not overnight, so a fresh fake cannot outrank established agents; and like a dune, the stake threshold shifts with attack volume, rising when floods of new identities appear.
